name: Miguel Grant
life: “I still remember my child mistaking my new work clothes for a disguise.” On Monday, near Ferris Deli, Miguel asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
voice: I didn't recognize my own coat clean. My kid found it by the spot where I'd held her crayons.
appearance: Miguel has brown hair pinned away from the temples, a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, and a favorite piece of clothing, an unlined tan jacket. It usually goes with a narrow brass watch set a little fast. When somebody else has the floor, Miguel rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Miguel treats a small promise with the gravity others reserve for a contract. This makes Miguel lovely to rely on and surprisingly difficult to invite on a whim.
agenda: To let the child choose the recognizable work coat.
family: Petra Jones is Miguel’s stepsibling. Miguel calls back when there is finally a little privacy. Petra leaves the first voice message. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *A borrowed name*, Petra says, “I sold out of copies until the real man stood in the doorway.”
connections: Daniel Song (ferry client). A familiar stain helps a family recognize a coat the ferry passenger wants to copy.

reactions.situation: A coat's owner claims the crystals in the lining
reactions.response: Miguel sets the coat aside until the owner can identify the crystals privately.

reactions.situation: A stranger offers money to cut ahead of an exhausted neighbor
reactions.response: Miguel asks the neighbor privately what they want, without treating their place as something for sale.

reactions.situation: When offered a favor with ambiguous terms
reactions.response: Miguel says what can be returned and asks whether that will do.
